transcript.text: Bosch built-in microwave BFL524MS0B randomly stops part way through cooking, time still on the display. Opening and closing the door lets it carry on. Maybe once every few days.

This is a frustrating but relatively common issue with built-in microwaves, particularly Bosch models like the BFL524MS0B. The fact that opening and closing the door allows it to continue is the critical diagnostic clue.

Here’s what is likely happening, ranked from most to least probable:

### 1. Door Switch/Latch Microswitch Issue (Most Likely)
Microwaves have multiple safety microswitches inside the door latch mechanism. One of these switches tells the control board "the door is closed and locked." If this switch is slightly faulty, worn out, or has a poor electrical connection:
• The microwave may momentarily lose contact with the "door closed" signal during operation (due to vibration, thermal expansion, or minor shifting).
• The control board interprets this as the door being opened → it pauses the magnetron and stops the timer display update (but keeps time visible because the clock is separate from the cooking function).
• When you open/close the door again, you physically reset the switch contact, re-establishing the "door closed" signal, allowing cooking to resume.

Why it happens randomly: It may only fail when:
• The turntable motor vibrates at a certain frequency.
• The food is heavy and shifts, causing slight vibration in the cavity.
• Thermal expansion of the plastic housing affects switch alignment after 10–20 minutes of heating.

### 2. Loose Wiring or Connector to Door Switches
The wiring harness connecting the door switches to the main control board may have a loose pin or corroded connector. Vibration during cooking can cause an intermittent connection loss, mimicking a "door open" signal.

### 3. Control Board Glitch (Less Likely but Possible)
The main PCB might be misinterpreting signals due to:
• A failing relay on the board that controls power to the magnetron.
• Software/firmware glitch causing false door-state detection.
However, since physically resetting the door fixes it, this is less likely than a hardware switch issue.

---

### ✅ What You Can Do Now (Temporary Workarounds)
1. Check Door Alignment: Ensure the door closes fully and evenly. If the hinges are loose or the door sags, it may not engage the switches properly under vibration. Tighten hinge screws if accessible.
2. Avoid Overfilling/Unbalanced Loads: Heavy or unevenly distributed food can cause more vibration during rotation, potentially triggering the switch issue.
3. Note the Pattern: Does it happen at a specific time (e.g., always after 10 mins)? This helps confirm if thermal expansion is a factor.

---

### 🔧 Recommended Solution: Professional Repair
Since this involves high-voltage components and safety interlocks, you should not attempt to open the microwave casing yourself unless you are qualified. The capacitor inside can hold a lethal charge even when unplugged.

Steps:
1. Contact Bosch Customer Service or an Authorized Servicer.
• Model: BFL524MS0B
• Issue: "Microwave pauses during cooking; door open/close resets it. Suspected door microswitch fault."
2. Ask specifically to check the door latch assembly and its microswitches. This is a common wear item and often covered under warranty if your unit is still eligible (check purchase date).
3. If out of warranty, this repair is usually straightforward and cost-effective compared to replacement: replacing the door switch or entire latch mechanism typically costs £50–£150 including labor, depending on your region.

### ⚠️ Safety Warning
• Do not bypass the door switches. This is extremely dangerous as it allows microwave energy to escape while in use.
• If the microwave ever starts sparking inside or smells of burning plastic, stop using it immediately and disconnect power.

This is almost certainly a door switch/latch mechanism issue, which is repairable and not indicative of a major internal failure like the magnetron.
